_why: Mutant ids DECLARED for PowerControlSetpoints. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object and a declared mutant LEAVES THE DENOMINATOR, so every entry is a claim somebody has to be able to answer. 47 of 76 are declared here and that number is alarming on its face, so READ THE SPLIT BEFORE THE SCORE: 39 of the 47 are NOT equivalent and are NOT unreachable -- they are KILLED, by one of this unit's two other oracles, with the mismatch count named in the entry. Only 8 are unkilled by anything, and NONE of the 8 is in a statement transcribed from the Fortran: every mutant in the unit's twenty reference statements is killed by the 3648-case differential harness, 0 survivors.
_the_honest_number: 68 of 76 behavioural mutants are killed by an instrument: 29 by the differential harness (harness/PowerControlSetpoints.json, 3648 cases), 36 by the list-directed format oracle (evidence/PowerControlSetpoints/ld_probe.txt, 22,526 gfortran records), 3 by the unit-401 file oracle (evidence/PowerControlSetpoints/f401_mutants.json). 8 are declared below. mutation/PowerControlSetpoints.harness-only.json is the same sweep with nothing declared: 29/76 = 0.3816, which is the harness's number ALONE and is the one to quote when asking what one instrument is worth here.
_tool_gap: `vit_mutate.py` has ONE bucket for `not killed by me`, and this unit needs two: `equivalent or unreachable` and `killed by another named oracle`. Writing the second into --equivalences is the only way to record it, and it makes `equivalent_declared: 47` an OVERSTATEMENT of the field's own name -- 39 of those 47 are kills. Recorded in DECISIONS.md as a candidate for the Driver. `scripts/dbgmutate.py` solved the same problem for unit #31 by replacing the oracle wholesale; this unit needs the union of three, which nothing in the pipeline expresses.
_measurement: evidence/PowerControlSetpoints/ld_survivor_census.txt is the reading behind the eight declarations, taken over the same 22,526 gfortran records the oracle uses: body length equals the field width in 0 of 22,526 records (widths seen: F 18/19/20 in a field of 21, E 23/24 and non-finite 8 in a field of 26); the stripped exponent is 1, 2 or 3 digits and is NEVER "0" and NEVER longer than 3.
028bf60f: index_offset '[512]' -> '[512 + 1]' at `char tmp[512]`, the scratch buffer `snprintf` writes the two conversions into. EQUIVALENT ON EVERY INPUT: the longest thing ever written there is a 24-character `%.16E` conversion, and both 512 and 513 are `snprintf`'s stated bound, which it respects. No input can make a program with 512 bytes of scratch differ from one with 513. This is a property of the buffer being over-sized, not of the corpus -- and the buffer is over-sized on purpose, copied from debug.cpp's `put_f`/`put_es`, where the same 512 stands.

The two differ only where the loop would consume the LAST remaining digit, i.e. where the stripped exponent is "0". UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by corpus: the E-form is entered only when the decimal exponent is < -1 or > 16, so an exponent of zero never reaches this loop. MEASURED at 0 of 22,526 records (ld_survivor_census.txt: `edig == "0"` 0). With `>=` and an all-zero exponent the loop would empty the string and `edig[0]` would read a past-the-end character -- undefined rather than wrong -- which is the reason the tight form is the one written.
1b6210f3: const_tweak '3' -> '4' at `if (edig.size() > 3)`, the refusal that fills the field with '*' when the exponent needs more digits than `Ee` allows. UNREACHABLE BY THE TYPE: a finite IEEE double's decimal exponent runs -324 .. 308, so the stripped exponent is at most 3 digits and NEITHER predicate is ever true. Measured: `edig longer than 3 digits` 0 of 22,526 (ld_survivor_census.txt), on a corpus that includes both representable extremes and every decade between them. The arm is dead for any input the C type admits, which is stronger than dead on a corpus. NOT REMOVED: `Ee` overflow is Fortran's rule and debug.cpp's `put_es` carries the same arm, where a narrower `e` makes it live.
